predecessors.note: Exiled Sienese loyalists reconstitute the Republic at Montalcino after the fall of Siena.

land.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

successors.note: Montalcino annexed by the Medici state in 1559 (Siena page: 'Tuscan troops arrived and annexed Montalcino, too').

capitals.name: Montalcino
capitals.note: My reading: the page places the exiled republic 'in Montalcino' and does not name a seat within it.

correction.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'a Republic of Siena reconstituted in Montalcino run by exiled Sienese loyalists continued to exist until 3 April 1559'. No page opened says how much land beyond the town it held; a 15 km radius round Montalcino is my reading (confidence 2). Cliopatria has no row for it.

region.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

ledger.note: 1555: exiled Sienese loyalists keep the Republic alive at Montalcino. 'a Republic of Siena reconstituted in Montalcino run by exiled Sienese loyalists continued to exist until 3 April 1559'; the Siena page: Montalcino 'did not concede defeat' after Marciano. The page gives no month for the founding; April follows the fall of Siena.

region.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

ledger.note: 1555: Montalcino holds out against the Medici conquerors. Montalcino page: 'Once Siena had been conquered by Florence under the rule of the Medici family in 1555', Montalcino 'held out for almost four years'. The Florence ledger records the same contest.

region.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

ledger.note: 3 April 1559: France recognises the Florentine conquest of Siena at Cateau-Cambresis. 'France recognised the 1555 conquest of the Republic of Siena' by Florence; History of Siena gives the end of the Montalcino republic as 31 May 1559, 'betrayed by the French allies'.

region.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

ledger.note: 1559: Montalcino passes to Florence. 'continued to resist Tuscan rule until 1559, when Tuscan troops arrived and annexed Montalcino, too'. The page has no month; the war page's 3 April is used.

region.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

ledger.note: 3 April 1559: the Republic of Siena in Montalcino ends. 'continued to exist until 3 April 1559'.

wars.name: Italian War of 1551-1559

zones.text: Montalcino, where the exiled Sienese government held out

wars.outcome: The Montalcino rump of Siena outlasted the fall of Siena by four years and was annexed by Florence under the terms of Cateau-Cambresis (3 April 1559).
wars.note: The war's main Siena phase is in the republic-of-siena dossier.

certainty.note: The pages name only the town; the land held around it is a radius.

sources.title: Republic of Siena
sources.note: Montalcino held out until 1559 and was then annexed.

sources.title: History of Siena
sources.note: Gives 31 May 1559 for the end of the Montalcino republic.

sources.title: Montalcino
sources.note: Held out almost four years after 1555.

notes: A four-year rump of the Republic of Siena, written as its own short dossier because the Florence ledger (eu-13-i) names 'Republic of Siena in Montalcino' as a counterpart; the main dossier is republic-of-siena. The page budget was the same four pages as Siena's, none of them the rump's own article, whose title I did not open (wikipedia and wikidata are null). Unsettled: the land held around Montalcino, the founding month, and the end date (3 April 1559 on the war page, 31 May 1559 on History of Siena, 'until 1559' on the Siena page).
